label: Contingent actual root: a brute contingent foundation
definition: ContingentRootAt m w holds when some concrete candidate exists at w, has no concrete ground existing at w under the selected relation at w, and is absent from some world accessible from w. Ordinary meaning: something concrete is there, could have failed to be there, and nothing concrete grounds it. Example: an initial physical state that simply exists. It is not uncaused under every relation: an abstract, absent or unmodelled explanation is not excluded.
note: Analyst framework definition of a rival position; attribution deferred. Motivated by brute-fact views of contingent reality and by existential inertia. Rival of EveryContingentGroundedAt on the same Profile and world: it asserts an instance that premise forbids, and with excluded middle it is equivalent to its negation (existing theorem everyContingentGrounded_iff_noContingentRoot). The Lean declaration predates this record; no earlier statement used it. 'Brute' is relative to the selected relation only (DEF-BRUTE-ROOT-RELATIVE-GROUNDING).
